locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_signed_mellin_round16.md · Statement and distinction from absolute sampling
statement: The ordinary inclusive symmetric height sum over nontrivial zeta zeros counted with multiplicity converges to the ordinary compensated Guinand–Weil formula with critical Mellin strip area weight √(1+t²). Consequently the logarithmic weights √(1+t²) log^p(e+|t|) suffice for every p≥0 under the same local hypotheses.
hypotheses: Continuous f with f(x)=O(x^δ) at zero and O(x^(−1−δ)) at infinity, F(u)=e^(u/2)f(e^u) in H¹ on a neighborhood of 0, and a finite stated strip norm on β∈[−ε,1+ε], 0<ε<δ. Unconditional. The contour proof establishes symmetric convergence, with separate half-axis convergence established by the Selberg route for p>1.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_signed_mellin_round16.md · Literal local hypotheses and the independent Selberg route
statement: For p>1, writing H(t)=h(1/2+it), Σ_ρ|h(ρ)−H(Im ρ)|<∞. If S₀(t)=N(t)−M(t) is the right-continuous positive-height counting remainder, then ∫₂∞|H′(t)S₀(t)|dt<∞ and H(T)S₀(T)→0 at every height. The same control holds with H(−t) on the negative half-axis.
hypotheses: Original endpoint value bounds and finite logarithmic Mellin strip area norm with p>1 and positive strip margin. Neither local H¹ nor a smooth-density convergence assumption is needed. The lemma does not address the projected term ∫ H M′.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_signed_mellin_round16.md · Literal local hypotheses and the independent Selberg route
statement: For p>1 the same signed zero sum converges separately on each half-height axis. The uniform density bound makes the projection onto Re s=1/2 an absolutely summable correction. The second moment of the counting remainder handles the signed Stieltjes integral, including the exact ordinate endpoint.
hypotheses: Same value, local H¹ and strip hypotheses as the symmetric theorem but with weight √(1+t²) log^p(e+|t|), p>1. No separate half-axis conclusion at p≤1 is asserted.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_signed_mellin_round16.md · Literal local hypotheses and the independent Selberg route
statement: Under the pinned manuscript's literal conditions (A) and (B), finite critical strip norm gives central F∈H¹⁄². Its Gagliardo seminorm excludes any genuine jump. The source midpoint values then select the continuous representative, and finite one-sided limits of f′ give local H¹ near x=1, so the critical symmetric formula applies.
hypotheses: Pinned 12-page Michigan author manuscript only. Condition (A) places the first-kind restriction on both f and f′ at its exceptional points. The general continuous class with the same value bounds needs a separate local assumption.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_signed_mellin_round16.md · A counterexample when the local-origin condition is omitted
statement: A real continuous compactly supported f, smooth off x=1, has finite p=3 logarithmic strip norm and symmetric raw-height sum tending to positive infinity. Its local archimedean compensation diverges. In log coordinates take a compact positive-definite multiplier times the inverse Fourier transform of a positive even spectrum comparable to 1/(|t| log²|t| loglog|t|). The smooth counting density diverges positively while the signed projection and count-remainder corrections converge.
hypotheses: Any fixed finite strip of the indicated form. The cusp lies outside literal (A) and the neighborhood H¹ theorem. It is separate from the smooth p=3 example of absolute divergence and supplies no additional author finding.

statement: For integer μ,ν≥1, z>1, M=μ+ν and L=log z, the unsigned log-power divisor sum differs from μ!ν!/(M+1)! times zL^(M+1) by at most [min(μ,ν)+1/e+μ^μν^ν/M^M] zL^M.
hypotheses: Gonek Lemma 7 (40), both derivative orders positive. The sign (−1)^(μ+ν) multiplies both parts in the Dirichlet series convention. The counting sum includes the integer endpoint. No claim of optimality or full numerical derivative-tail bound.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_gonek_constants_round16.md · A convenient rational (1,1) allocation and its finite use
statement: For the (1,1) coefficient B_n in Gonek Lemma 8, letting L=log x and I₃=∫₁ˣ u^(iδ−1) log³(x/u)du, the finite error |Σ_(n≤x) B_n(1,1,δ)+(x/6)I₃| is at most x[(19/4)L³+(229/4)L²+90L].
hypotheses: Real x>1 and real |δ|≤1/2. Uses the convenient rational (1,1) convolution bound 9/4 and the positive-power Abel specialization with vanishing upper boundary. This concerns only the divisor and prime-to-integral steps.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_riemann1859_whole_round16.md · Continuation and the product: the exact missing steps
statement: Let Xi(t)=ξ_*(1/2+it), with ξ_*(s)=s(s−1)π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2)ζ(s)/2. Its even Taylor series defines G(w)=Xi(√w), entire of order at most 1/2 by log M_Xi(R)=O(R log(R+2)), with order exactly 1/2 by Stirling along positive real s. Hadamard gives the genus-zero product Xi(t)=Xi(0) ∏_(Re α>0)(1−t²/α²), including multiplicities. In s coordinates the paired normalization is Xi(0)∏_α(1+1/(4α²))=ξ_*(0)=1/2.
hypotheses: Riemann's theta and cosine representations, evenness, positivity on the imaginary t axis, and external modern finite-order Hadamard factorization. No RH, square-root branch choice, or zero-count asymptotic is used for the product. This is a known modern reconstruction of the 1859 product.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_riemann1859_whole_round16.md · Exact arithmetic identity, branches and the known constant
statement: For x>1, midpoint J₀(x) equals li(x)−lim_(T→∞)Σ_(|Im ρ|≤T) E_ρ(x)+∫ₓ∞du/[u(u²−1)log u]−log 2. Use E_ρ(x)=Ei(ρ log x)−iπ sgn(Im ρ) with the continued log x^ρ=ρ log x. The offsets cancel under conjugate ordering. The summable O_I((1+|Im ρ|)^(−2)) kernel remainder reduces raw pointwise convergence to the later von Mangoldt midpoint ψ₀ formula. Unit-height counts and O_x(1/T) terms give equivalence with the source's |α| order.
hypotheses: Midpoint values at prime powers, zeros with multiplicity, the stated height order, paired normalization, and external later ordered von Mangoldt formula. The real constant −log 2 is Genocchi's known correction. No proof of the ordered limit is attributed to the 1859 text and no novelty is claimed.
